Subject: Hosting carveout for pilot + DPA redline

Hi Rohan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — our engineering team is keen to start a short EU pilot next month. We ran into a hardware availability constraint in our EU cloud region and would like to scope a limited pilot that routes model inference to a US-hosted cluster for the next 8 weeks.

Before we proceed we need to confirm two things from a legal/compliance perspective:
1) Confirmation that Redwood can accept a temporary hosting carveout for the pilot (EU data residency exception) and the associated temporary SCCs amendment.
2) A redline to the DPA showing the temporary transfer impact addendum and a list of technical/operational safeguards you will apply (KV cache controls, transcript retention, KMS key residency if any).

I've attached a proposed DPA redline from our side (HealthCo_DPA_redline_20270411.docx) and a short pilot scope spreadsheet. Can you loop in the right people at Redwood to confirm feasibility and timeline? We need a legal touchpoint by Wednesday 4/14 to keep procurement on schedule.

Hi team and Emma —

Thanks for the clear ask, Emma. Quick commercial/legal plan below:

Proposed approach (high level):
- Approve a limited "pilot exception" that permits EU-origin traffic to be served from a US cluster for a strictly bounded 8-week window.
- Put the exception into an addendum (Pilot Hosting Addendum) that references the DPA and SCCs amendment.
- Apply the following technical commitments during the pilot:
  * Only hashed request IDs are stored; conversational KV cache rotated hourly.
  * Retention window: 30 days for logs; inference transcripts will not be persisted beyond session lifespan unless explicitly consented.
  * KMS: customer-managed keys are unsupported for this pilot; we will document the control plane access and logging.
  * Enhanced auditing: daily export of request logs to a secured S3 bucket (accessible to HealthCo audit team on request).

Attached is a preliminary Redwood redline (SCCs_template_v2.pdf referenced) and a suggested clause for the Pilot Hosting Addendum. If Legal approves the clause wording, I can issue an internal Exec Approval request and then send a DocuSign packet to HealthCo.

Next steps / asks:
- @laura_bennett: please review the addendum clause and DPA redline and advise whether the proposed controls are sufficient from a GDPR/transfer perspective.
- @irene_choi: privacy ops — can your team commit to the retention and logging controls above for the 8-week period? Any telemetry/evidence we should produce up front?
- Emma: can you confirm whether HealthCo's legal team will accept an addendum + temporary SCCs amendment or whether they need a full execution of Standard Contractual Clauses separately?

Attachments (stubs):
- Redwood_Pilot_Hosting_Addendum_draft.docx (attachment)
- SCCs_template_v2.pdf (attachment)

Best,

Ben / Rohan / Emma —

Thanks, Ben. I reviewed the proposed Pilot Hosting Addendum and HealthCo's redline. High-level input:

1) Temporary carveout is acceptable provided we:
   - Limit scope to a named test environment and specific accounts in the pilot (we should enumerate project IDs).
   - Include an explicit end-date and an auto-reversion clause that reverts routing to EU-only hosting at the end of the pilot.

2) DPA redline: we should counter on two points:
   - KMS language: we cannot commit to customer-managed keys for this pilot. Insert wording that keys remain Redwood-managed; we can provide audit logs of key operations.
   - Subprocessor list: add a paragraph requiring notification within 5 business days of any subprocessor changes during the pilot.

3) SCCs amendment: acceptable as a limited addendum, but we should add a carveout paragraph stating the amendment applies only to the Pilot Hosting Addendum and does not alter broader data residency obligations post-pilot.

Draft edits I propose (short):
- Section 2.1 (Scope): add project IDs or account IDs — ACTION: Rohan, please share the account/project IDs for HealthCo's pilot.
- Section 5.4 (Termination): add auto-reversion and verification audit clause.

If these edits are fine with Privacy, I will prepare a clean counter-redline and legal mark-up and ask for a quick Exec approval. We will also produce an evidence bundle (logs, daily audit extracts) to HealthCo for the pilot start.

Laura Bennett
General Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Hi all —

Privacy/ops can meet the proposed commitments with the following clarifications:
- Retention: logs and non-persisted transcripts will be retained for 30 days; we will flag the HealthCo pilot tenant in our retention engine so reversion is automated.
- Auditing: we will generate daily CSV audit extracts covering request meta (timestamp, region served, request_id hash) and store them in the HealthCo-specified secure bucket; provide read-only access for up to 30 days after pilot end.
- Subprocessors: operations will produce a signed subprocessor ledger for the pilot and commit to 5 business day notification for changes.
- KMS: cannot support customer-managed KMS for this short pilot; we will include detailed KMS operation logs and a key use audit.

Laura — with your edits, Privacy can fast-track the evidence bundle. Rohan — please confirm the pilot account/project IDs and intended start date (we need at least 48 hours lead time to configure retention flags).

Thanks,
